messages.subject: Re: [dartR] gl.report.heterozygosity assumes SNP data are from SilicoDArT?

messages.body_plain:
Hi John,

Thank you for trying those two scripts I posted. From what I can see, the compliance check (and other scripts that check for the type of data) are finding only scores of 0 and 1, confirming the assumption that the data are presence absence data. In SNP datasets, one would expect a smattering of 0's (homozygous ref), 1's (heterozygotes) and 2's (homozygous alternate).

Then when the scripts check the ploidy of the dataset after the compliance check, they find ploidy=2, which suggests that the data are SNP data.

These conflicting signals are confusing our scripts.

I am unable to get to the root of the problem without having access to your data. Would you be willing to use saveRDS(genlight,"testset.Rdata") and post testset.Rdata for me to look at? Or send it to geo...@aerg.canberra.edu.au.

Arthur

messages.subject: Re: filtering on HWE departure
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

We have updated the report and filter functions to test for Hardy-Weinberg proportions. To use these updated functions you should install the dev version of dartR as described below.
Now the functions gl.report.hwe and gl.filter.hwe have the same options and give the same results.
- These updated functions test for H-W proportions using either the Exact or the Chi-square method.
- Adjustment for multiple comparisons can be applied by using 5 different methods.
- Ternary plots have been updated using the R package "ggtern", which should be installed and loaded for these plots to work.

# library required to install from github
library(devtools)
# installing developing version of dartR
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
# if you are working with R-studio restart your session with menu Session -> Restart R
library(dartR)
test <- gl.report.hwe(bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl>)
test_2 <- gl.filter.hwe(bandicoot.gl <http://bandicoot.gl>)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.subject: Re: Error found in gl.report.heterozygosity
messages.body_plain:
Hi Gabriella,

You are right in your observation: DArT uses 0 for the reference homozygote, 1 for SNP homozygote and 2 for heterozygote. Conversely, dartR uses 0 for the reference homozygote, 1 for heterozygote and 2 for SNP homozygote.
When you read your DArT report into dartR using for example the function gl.read.dart(), the numbers are for each genotype are changed, this is so for at least two reasons:
(a) It is the coding schema used by the package Adegenet, so it is difficult to move from this while maintaining access to all the Adegenet features;
(b) It allows summing the codes to obtain the frequency of SNP's, which simplifies greatly the computational side of things.

This information is documented in the manuals and vignettes of dartR.

Please let us know whether this information solved your question.

Cheers,
Luis
